source.title: Automated Natural Language Explanation of Deep Visual Neurons with Large Models
source.authors: Chenxu Zhao; Wei Qian; Yucheng Shi; Mengdi Huai; Ninghao Liu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure content is flattened, but the relevant ablation result is also stated in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies explanations and ablations of visual-network units, but does not test any listed claim version. It cites the language-model neuron-explanation paper without testing its findings.
record.gate_note: The paper gives qualitative neuron-explanation examples and describes agreement with human annotations, but reports no quantitative explanation-accuracy score. Those results do not test the listed versions. The text reports an 84% category-accuracy drop for one ablated unit and shows maximum category-accuracy-drop plots for two models; these concern neuron importance, not the listed claims, so they are recorded with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a CLIP+GPT method to label vision-network units and shows qualitative examples and single-unit ablations. It reports no share of interpretable neurons and no comparison across tools or architectures. It does not score explanations by predicting held-out activations. Bills et al. is cited only in the introduction. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude their automated LLM+VLM method produces neuron explanations agreeing with human labels across architectures and datasets, and that semantically labelled units matter for specific categories. The agreement claim rests on qualitative examples only, with no agreement metric reported.
record.recipe_differences: This is a visual-neuron explanation method: it selects activated image patches, uses GPT-3 to create a concept vocabulary, and uses CLIP to match concepts to patches. It does not use the language-model neuron explanation audit method.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating a ResNet50-ImageNet layer4 unit labelled as mashed-avocado dip dropped guacamole accuracy by 84%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single semantically labelled units in late CNN layers can be critical for specific categories.

fits_no_version.finding: Plots of maximum per-category accuracy drop are shown for the top 256 units in ResNet layer4 and AlexNet conv5, without numbers in the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unit importance to individual categories varies across units in late CNN layers.

record.problems: The explanation-quality evidence is primarily qualitative; no quantitative explanation score or uncertainty is reported. The plotted ablation results have no numerical values in the text, and the stated 84% example is not accompanied by uncertainty or a baseline accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: Qualitative neuron-explanation examples in Figures 2 and 3 and the general statement of agreement with human descriptions were not made into rows: the paper does not report separate quantitative outcomes for those examples.

untested.parts: All parts: language-model shares across families and scale.
All parts: InceptionV1 polysemantic neurons and pose.
All parts: interpretable share by tool or architecture. Only a few selected units across AlexNet, ResNet50 and ViT are shown qualitatively, with no share reported.
All parts: no test of whether explanations predict held-out activations. Explanations are derived from top-activating patches only.

record.verdict_notes: The abstract says quantitative analysis was done, but the only quantitative results are the ablation accuracy drops. There is no explanation-quality score, so nothing bears on V6 or V7.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole shares and the proportions of single-job, related-job, and not-yet-understood poles.
Language-model shares across model families, dense or mixture-of-experts architectures, and scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose as their shared feature, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
The paper does not compare interpretability shares across tools, architectures, or regularization choices, or give the stated InceptionV1-sized-model estimates.
The paper does not build attribution graphs or test whether they explain model behavior without a replacement model or reconstruction error.
The paper does not test whether explanations based on activating examples predict activations on separate examples.
The paper does not score explanations by simulating neuron activations on new text.

rows.subject: ResNet50-ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Ablated one unit by setting its feature-map weights and biases to 0.
rows.measure: Test accuracy drop for the category
rows.note: The paper says the unit represents a dip or spread made from mashed avocado. The model and unit are identified in the figure; the text reports the 84% drop.
rows.check: This measures the importance of one hand-picked unit to one category, not interpretability shares or explanation accuracy. No baseline accuracy is given. The example was selected, so it is illustrative rather than a population result.
